summary: The starter prompt plus the supplied run-environment skill.md and the installed DocumentDB skills give a clear high-level goal: a Node.js LangChain conversational agent that reads/writes slot and appointment documents and does atomic reschedules. Enough is present to start implementation, but many concrete choices (driver version, exact schema, APIs/entrypoint, LLM model, seed data, tests, README and infra-as-code) are left to the builder and will be chosen by reasonable defaults unless the author clarifies them.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js LangChain agent ... that query DocumentDB for provider availability slots, create appointment documents, and handle rescheduling by updating slot status atomically."
rubric.note: High-level business goal and scenario are explicit in the prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Node.js LangChain agent with agent memory and tools"
rubric.note: Single-agent, LangChain, with tools and memory is explicitly requested.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Node.js" and from skill.md: "Node.js 24 with npm and npx is available."
rubric.note: Runtime version is provided in the sample's run-environment (skill.md).

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the official 'mongodb' npm package (latest stable major at build time, pinned in package.json), and follow the documentdb-driver guidance to create a singleton MongoClient.
rubric.note: The documentdb-driver skill gives the pattern (singleton client) and guidance but does not mandate an exact driver version; the builder will pick a reasonable recent driver and pin it.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN, HNSW and IVF vector indexes) is reachable ..." (skill.md)
rubric.note: Run-environment explicitly names the live cluster and tier to use; do not provision another cluster.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Its connection string is in the environment variable `DOCUMENTDB_URI`. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or `.env.example` with a placeholder, as the prompt asks." (skill.md)
rubric.note: Secrets location (env var) is specified; driver skill also recommends SCRAM-SHA-256 and TLS.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Provider availability is modelled as slot documents ... booking creates an appointment document ..."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create database 'sample_healthcare_05' (skill.md) with collections 'slots' and 'appointments'. slots documents: {_id, providerId, start: ISODate, end: ISODate, status: 'available'|'booked'|'cancelled', metadata: {...}}. appointments documents: {_id, patientId, slotId, status, createdAt, notes}. No explicit shard key (single-shard/small sample).
rubric.note: Conceptual model is stated, but exact field names, types, indexes and relationships are left to the implementer; documentdb-data-modeling gives guidance.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will supply a small idempotent seed script (e.g., seed.js) that upserts a few providers, slots for multiple times, and one or two appointments for demo purposes.
rubric.note: No sample data source, size, license or idempotent loader is specified or covered by skills. documentdb-local-deployment discusses sample-data tooling but doesn't provide sample content.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "tools that query DocumentDB for provider availability slots" and atomic updates to slot status
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement queries to find slots by providerId and time range and create an index such as { providerId: 1, start: 1, status: 1 } to support those queries. For atomic updates the code will use a conditional update or a transaction as described in the prompt.
rubric.note: The prompt requires the behavior but leaves index shapes and parameters to the implementer; documentdb-indexing provides guidance for picking indexes.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "LangChain agent" is requested but no chat/embedding model or provider is specified.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will wire LangChain to a commonly used chat model (e.g., OpenAI-compatible model via env var OPENAI_API_KEY) and document the required env vars in .env.example. No embeddings are strictly required for booking/rescheduling conversational context (use LangChain conversation memory), so embedding model selection can be omitted unless the builder adds semantic search.
rubric.note: Model provider and exact model/dimensions are not specified; that will change how the LangChain agent is configured.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js LangChain agent ... so a patient can say 'move it an hour later'"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will expose a simple HTTP API (Express) with a /chat endpoint that accepts conversational messages and returns agent responses; developer CLI tooling (scripts) may be included for local interactive testing. The agent's tools will be implemented as LangChain Tools invoked by the agent during processing.
rubric.note: Prompt implies conversational interface but does not mandate an HTTP API vs CLI vs web UI; the choice affects example client and README.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned... Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use." (skill.md)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: No infra provisioning will be included; builder will operate against the existing cluster.
rubric.note: An infra-as-code artifact is not requested; the run-environment explicitly provides the live cluster to use.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add a README with commands: npm install, npm run seed, npm start, and a demo interaction. Tests will be runnable via npm test with mocked DB clients.
rubric.note: No concrete run or test commands were provided.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat successful demo interactions that (1) query available slots, (2) create a booking and mark slot booked, (3) reschedule atomically to a new available slot when asked relative times, and (4) cancel an appointment returning slot to available as the criteria for done.
rubric.note: Prompt states desired behaviors but doesn't provide an acceptance checklist; the implementer will create one.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use." (skill.md)
rubric.note: The run environment limits writes to provisioning; otherwise cost/DR constraints are not enumerated.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will follow common Node sample conventions: package.json, src/, scripts/ (seed.js, start script), .env.example, README.md and tests/ with mocks. Dependencies pinned in package.json; lockfile (package-lock.json) included.
rubric.note: No explicit repo layout, README section list or dependency-pinning rule is given.

questions_for_author: Which LLM/chat provider and model should the LangChain agent use (e.g., OpenAI gpt-4, gpt-4o-mini, or an on-prem model)? This changes env vars and example configuration.

Should the sample expose an HTTP API endpoint (e.g., Express /chat) for conversational clients, provide a CLI demo, or include a small web UI? The choice affects included client/demo code and README instructions.

Do you require a seed script, unit tests that run without a live cluster (mocks), and infrastructure-as-code for the DocumentDB cluster? The prompt's run environment supplies a cluster, but gallery standards often also want these artifacts.
requirements_at_risk: A `.env.example` lists every setting with placeholder values — not specified in the prompt or covered by skills.
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output — embedding model/dimensions are not specified, so any vector index choices are at risk.
The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one — no guidance provided.
A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — sample data loader is not specified.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — the sample doesn't request a search endpoint, so this behavior is unlikely to be implemented.
Search results include the similarity score — not applicable unless semantic search is added; at risk if gallery expects this.
Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt` — for a Node project, dependency pinning and a lockfile need explicit instruction; not specified.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — no instruction to include tests with mocked DBs, so this may be missing.
Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — the run environment provides a cluster and the prompt forbids provisioning; IaC is not included.
The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — README contents are not specified and may be incomplete.
The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout — not enforced by the prompt; implementer might use different product names unless instructed.
